newsitem.title: UK: Coffee trade wants USDA to clarify Brazil data.
newsitem.headline: Coffee trade wants USDA to clarify Brazil data.

text.p: Several European coffee traders on Wednesday urged the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) to clarify apparently conflicting Brazil 1997/98 coffee crop forecasts.
"I'm finding it difficult to give a meaning to it," said one Dutch trader. "It's strange to see two people from the same organisation giving different ideas."

A field report by a U.S. agricultural attache in Sao Paulo dated May 12 was made public on Tuesday in which the attache saw the 1997/98 harvest at 24 million bags versus 27.5 million bags the previous year.
On June 13, a USDA estimate put it at 28 million bags.
This forecast caused an outcry within Brazil because it conflicted with most trade views there of 23 million to 25 million bags and a government forecast of 22 million bags.
The view that this year's harvest might be bigger, if marginally, than last year's was also unprecedented.
Some other European traders, however, played down any idea of a controversy, saying that it was still early to gauge the size of the crop.

One London trader said: "The problem is everybody treating the USDA like a Bible...Crop forecasting is an imprecise science. In the case of Brazil, you have to add or minus three or four million tonnes."
